text:
Omar: Quick UX/a11y thread 1: selection toolbar and keyboard-range selection in regression diffs. We keep getting reports that keyboard users can't tell how many items are selected when using Shift+Arrow or Shift+Click. Need copy + announce behavior.

Maria: good catch. On desktop mouse users get a floating selection bar showing count and actions, but screen-reader users only hear individual focus changes. Proposal: add a persistent in-context selection toolbar that appears when selection_count > 0 with text 'n items selected' and actions 'Approve selected' / 'Clear selection'.

Jen: visual idea: toolbar should be attached to the top of the diff list (not bottom) so it doesn't cover last item. In compact mode make it slim and collapse extra actions into a kebab menu. For keyboard flow, when selection starts (Shift+Arrow) do NOT move focus; announce via aria-live that '3 items selected'.

Sam: accessibility checklist: 1) selection toolbar should be role="region" aria-label="Selection toolbar" and the live announcement should be polite, e.g. <div aria-live="polite">
2) when user adjusts selection range announce exact count and range: '3 items selected, items 50707 to 50909' (if list positions are stable). Avoid stealing focus.

Luca: analytics: track selection_start_method (shift_arrow|shift_click|click), selection_count, selection_range_start, selection_range_end, and whether approve_used_from_toolbar true/false. We want to see if keyboard users prefer toolbar or top-level bulk controls.

QA Bot: e2e note: /e2e/prompt-evals/selection-toolbar.spec.js currently fails because the toolbar is injected before the list in DOM, causing tab order issues. Test expects toolbar after header, before list. Also flaky when announce messages come too fast for headless SR.

Maria: microcopy suggestions for toolbar: primary label '3 items selected' (dynamic), primary CTA 'Approve selected', secondary 'Clear selection', tertiary 'View changes'. In confirm modal: title 'Approve 3 selected results?' body 'This will mark the selected results as expected for this prompt set. You can revert from regression history.' Primary CTA 'Approve 3 results'.

Jen: implementation notes: keep toolbar in DOM order above the list (so tab goes to toolbar first). For keyboard users who start selection mid-list, we should provide a skip link 'Skip to selection toolbar (press S)' that focuses toolbar. Also add visible focus outline for toolbar actions.

Sam: caution: using single-letter shortcuts like 'S' can conflict with page typing. Recommend Shift+S or Ctrl+Alt+S optionally. Document and provide help dialog. For screen reader announces, avoid verbose ranges unless user requests details, some SR users prefer concise counts. Maybe provide a second optional aria-live region with details triggered by a small help button.

Luca: analytics: include shortcut_used boolean and shortcut_key value so we can see adoption. Also record selection_cleared_by_user boolean.

QA Bot: test suggestions: 1) assert DOM order: header -> toolbar -> list -> footer; 2) assert aria-live message equals expected count string after selection; 3) simulate shift+arrow and verify announcement does not steal focus. Current flaky on Chrome headless should be resolved if toolbar is placed before list and aria-live timing adjusted.

Karen: tiny copy nit: instead of 'Clear selection' maybe 'Deselect all' reads better. Also prefer 'Approve selected' consistent across product.

Omar: good convo. Action items: Maria finalize copy tokens (i18n keys), Jen prototype toolbar placement and keyboard shortcut behavior, Sam add exact aria snippets and minimalist announce phrasing to PR, Luca wire analytics schema, QA to add/adjust e2e per suggestions. We'll review Wed 10am. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
